problem:
$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 1 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ t\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the system of differential equations. Using the method of variation of parameters, the general solution of the equation can be written in the form

| $x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+\,\,\frac{1}{9}$ |  | {{field-1}} |  | . |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | $23-15t$ |  |  |  |
worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

Notice that we are given that

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}.
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-3t} & {e}^{-t} \\ {e}^{-3t} & 3{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}3t \\ t\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{-3t}\cdot 3{e}^{-t}-{e}^{-t}\cdot {e}^{-3t}}[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{-t} & -{e}^{-t} \\ -{e}^{-3t} & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2{e}^{-4t}}[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{-t} & -{e}^{-t} \\ -{e}^{-3t} & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{3t} & -{e}^{3t} \\ -{e}^{t} & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{3t} & -{e}^{3t} \\ -{e}^{t} & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4t{e}^{3t} \\ -t{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}4t{e}^{3t} \\ -t{e}^{t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int 4t{e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int -t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating the components by parts, we get the following:

- For the first component, let $u=4t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=4\,\text{d}t$ and $v=\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4t{e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t & =(4t)\cdot \frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}-\int \frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}\cdot (4\,\text{d}t) \\  & =\frac{4}{3}t{e}^{3t}-\frac{4}{3}\int {e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{4}{3}t{e}^{3t}-\frac{4}{9}{e}^{3t} \\  & =\frac{4}{9}{e}^{3t}(3t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, let $u=-t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=-\,\text{d}t$ and $v={e}^{t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int -t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t & =(-t)\cdot {e}^{t}-\int {e}^{t}(-\,\text{d}t) \\  & =-t{e}^{t}+\int {e}^{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =-t{e}^{t}+{e}^{t} \\  & ={e}^{t}(1-t).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-3t} & {e}^{-t} \\ {e}^{-3t} & 3{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{9}{e}^{3t}(3t-1) \\ {e}^{t}(1-t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}4(3t-1)+9(1-t) \\ 4(3t-1)+27(1-t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}3t+5 \\ 23-15t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
